source: USDA NRCS, National Engineering Handbook Part 631, Chapter 3 'Engineering Classification of Earth Materials', Figure 3-22 'Engineering properties of USCS soil classes' (210-631-H, 2nd Ed., Jun 2022). PDF in the suite bibliography (Suelos/NRCS_NEH-631_Ch3_Engineering-Classification-of-Earth-Materials_USCS.pdf).
note: Shear strength, compressibility and workability are qualitative in the source table. Permeability is given as ranges. There are no numeric c/phi values in this official source; numeric parameter proposals are a separate spec with its own source.

GW.typical_names: Well-graded gravels, gravel-sand mixtures, little or no fines

GP.typical_names: Poorly graded gravels, gravel-sand mixtures, little or no fines

SW.typical_names: Well-graded sands, gravelly sands, little or no fines

SP.typical_names: Poorly graded sands, gravelly sands, little or no fines

ML.typical_names: Inorganic silts and very fine sands, rock flour, silty or clayey fine sands, or clayey silts with slight plasticity

CL.typical_names: Inorganic clays of low to medium plasticity, gravelly clays, sandy clays, silty clays, and lean clays

OL.typical_names: Organic silts and organic silty clays of low plasticity

MH.typical_names: Inorganic silts, micaceous or diatomaceous fine sandy or silty soils, elastic silts

CH.typical_names: Inorganic clays of high plasticity, fat clays

OH.typical_names: Organic clays of medium to high plasticity, organic silts

PT.typical_names: Peat and other highly organic soils
